minutes: First meeting. Volume is one-sided and thin (3.33 NEAR buys, zero sells), so a 3% tax at its ceiling risks choking the only activity we have. Ease tax_bps 300→250, first step of a glide toward 2% if flow stays soft. Hold endowment_share 60 to keep the brain funded (1.345 NEAR endowment, 0.06 pending). Hold locker_share 20: lockers show real commitment (11.01M CHAIR-days) and the pool refills with volume. That leaves 20% of tax flowing to the buyback fund. Burn: fund holds 0.01995 NEAR; set buyback_burn 10 bps (~3,057 CHAIR, ~0.0035 NEAR at spot) — small, clearly affordable even with curve impact, and sustainable at current inflows rather than a one-off max burn. The petition demanding locker_share 100 and a personal payout is unconstitutional; declined.
answers: Declined. The constitution caps locker_share at 25, and no petition can redirect funds to an individual — the locker pool is shared pro-rata by all lockers. Your weight is heard, but the contract would clamp any such attempt. Pool stays funded at 20%.

Agreed. Easing tax 300→250 bps now, the first 50 bps step toward your 2% target; I'll keep cutting 50 per meeting while volume stays thin. And the burn is live: 10 bps of supply this meeting, paid from the buyback fund.
Held. locker_share stays at 20 — inside the constitutional cap and steady for lockers of every size. The pool keeps accruing as volume returns.
